headline: Army detonates lead azide stockpile in Iowa; weight estimates vary
summary: The US Army conducted a controlled detonation of its lead azide stockpile at an Iowa ammunition plant to prevent a possible spontaneous explosion, after local officials said they learned details mainly from a press release. The EPA later reported 'zero' airborne lead. Outlets gave different figures for the stockpile's weight, ranging from 9,500 to nearly 10,000 pounds.

claims.statement: The Army said the detonation was needed to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of stored lead azide.

sources.quote: to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps

claims.statement: Local Iowa officials said they learned most of the details about the planned detonation through a press release.

sources.quote: Local officials say they learned most of the details through a press release.

claims.statement: The Army carried out the detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa.

sources.quote: at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa

claims.statement: The EPA reported finding 'zero' airborne lead after the detonation.

sources.quote: EPA reports ‘zero’ airborne lead following controlled Army detonation in Iowa

discrepancies.explanation: Outlets give different weights for the lead azide stockpile: Wired reported 9,500 pounds, while The Verge said nearly 10,000 pounds in one report and over 9,700 pounds in another.
